system.name: Helmsman
system.one_liner: a cost-effective, high-performance clustering-based approximate nearest-neighbor search (ANNS) system for large-scale vector retrieval

components.name: Memory Shard
components.role: one of several DRAM-resident shards that together hold the full HNSW graph when it exceeds a single shard's capacity

components.name: DRAM
components.role: holds all graph data (neighbor lists and raw vectors) for in-memory HNSW search

components.name: In-DRAM Graph Index
components.role: HNSW graph searched via greedy best-neighbor descent layer by layer, then a best-first search over a candidate pool at the bottom layer

components.name: Query Vector
components.role: the query embedding used to start the graph search

components.name: DRAM-SSD Node
components.role: a single node hosting a large-scale hybrid DRAM-SSD graph index to cut memory footprint

components.name: SSD
components.role: stores full-precision vectors and graph edges to reduce DRAM consumption

components.name: DRAM-SSD Graph Index
components.role: graph traversed with best-first search and beam search, fetching PQ-compressed/cached candidates from DRAM and full data from SSD in batches

flows.what: greedy best-neighbor descent from an entry node, layer by layer, then best-first search over a candidate pool at the bottom
best-first search with a beam-search procedure fetching candidates from SSD in batches

content.key_idea: Two prior ANNS designs trade off differently: an all-DRAM sharded HNSW graph gives the lowest latency, while a hybrid DRAM-SSD graph trades some latency for far lower memory footprint on a single node.
content.reading_order: Left panel (a) then right panel (b): each shows a query vector entering a graph index built on a different storage tier.

summary: This is a background figure from the Helmsman paper (an ANNS system built around clustering-based indexes) comparing two prior approaches used at RedNote for approximate nearest-neighbor search. Panel (a) shows an in-DRAM HNSW design: the full graph's neighbor lists and vectors are kept in DRAM, partitioned across multiple Memory Shards when too large for one node, and a query descends greedily from an entry node layer by layer before a best-first search over a candidate pool yields the top-k results, favoring low latency and high QPS. Panel (b) shows a hybrid DRAM-SSD Node design used for more latency-relaxed workloads like content moderation and RAG: PQ-compressed and frequently accessed vectors stay cached in DRAM while full-precision vectors and edges live on SSD, and a query uses best-first search with a beam-search width that controls batched SSD I/O.
summary_zh: Helmsman背景对比图,展示RedNote两种ANNS方案:(a)全内存HNSW跨Shard分片,逐层贪心搜索,低延迟;(b)DRAM-SSD混合方案,压缩/热点向量存DRAM、原始数据存SSD,beam-search批量读取省内存。
